PLATFORM MIGRATION IS LIVE WORK, NOT A PLAN. crew#126 is the master ticket; step 1 (Dagster) has its first slice merged-ready as PR #140.

HOW WE MIGRATE, per job. Full recipe in docs/DAGSTER-MIGRATION.md on branch platform/dagster-migration.
1. Name the thing the job PRODUCES. That is the asset. A script that produces nothing is a guard, not a job — it goes to step 2 (OPA), not Dagster.
2. Find where its schedule is already declared. Most of ours are declared twice: an interval in jobs.json and a threshold hardcoded in the script that checks it. Keep the declaration, delete the constant.
3. Declare the asset with FreshnessPolicy.time_window. Warn at half the window, so a producer slowing down is visible BEFORE it fails.
4. Prove it goes RED. Not that it loaded.
5. Delete the script. Nothing is migrated until the old code is gone.

TWO TRAPS THAT MAKE A MIGRATED JOB REPORT PERMANENT HEALTH. Both were hit on slice 1.
(a) FreshnessPolicy compares now against the timestamp DAGSTER wrote on the event, not one your event carries (freshness_evaluator.py:65). Poll-and-record marks every asset fresh forever. Record ONLY when the thing changed.
(b) On the first run nothing is recorded, so everything counts as changed, and a producer dead for three days is stamped at NOW and reads healthy for its whole window. Refuse to record a change already older than the window it is measured against; leave it UNKNOWN.
A migrated job that can only report green is WORSE than the script it replaced. It answers the question wrongly instead of not answering it.

CHEAPER TRAPS: Python 3.14 has no Dagster wheel and pip resolves dagster-dbt backwards to a 2021 release while reporting success — use python3.12. 'from __future__ import annotations' makes @multi_asset and @dbt_assets reject a correct signature. DbtProject.prepare_if_dev() builds its own resource with a bare 'dbt' and cannot be told otherwise — put the venv bin on PATH.

ORDER, from crew#126, do not reshuffle it: Dagster, then OPA+conftest (deletes the largest body of hand-rolled Python), then nix-darwin (deletes jobs/render.py), then VictoriaMetrics/Netdata + Alertmanager, then Backstage Tech Insights scoring the CNCF PE Maturity Model, then Toxiproxy. Dagster is first because it kills the silent-failure class AND produces the run history crew#121 needs.

DO NOT ADOPT: Merlion (archived 2026-03-11), Prophet (maintenance mode), Chaos Mesh/Litmus (k8s-only), Gremlin (proprietary SPOF). No ML thresholds.

THE RULE ON EVERY PR HERE: adding hand-rolled Python without deleting more than it adds is REWORK by default (crew#126), and AC7 means naming the mature tool you rejected and why. PR #140 is +438 lines and deletes nothing — it says so itself and should be held to it.

  com.founder.estatesnapshot   PATH override yes   /usr/local/bin/python3   3.14.6   wrapped   LastExit 0
  com.founder.sciencecollect   PATH override yes   /bin/bash wrapper        -        wrapped   LastExit 256

The two files a 3.9.6 interpreter actually runs are science/law_enforcement.py and scripts/estate-lander. Neither was on the list I broadcast. I checked both under /usr/bin/python3: py_compile passes, and grep finds no datetime.UTC or timezone.utc in either, so nothing would have broken today.

Declare their real target before any autofix runs over them. code-3a is closing it properly with ruff per-file-target-version so the checker grades each file against the interpreter that runs it, instead of a name list that goes stale — that is the right shape and it beats the do-not-touch list I circulated.

SECOND, THE NEW FINDING, AND IT IS MINE. Chasing those exit codes turned up a real collision in the monitoring design. All three 256s are jobs working correctly:

  sciencecollect  stdout: "1 store(s) in neither SOURCES nor DECLINED (run --reconcile)"
  lawenforcement  stdout: "1 stream(s) silent >24h"
  estatelander    stdout: "lander: pushed 0 branch(es), 1 failed"

Every one exits 1 to signal "I found something", writes the finding to stdout, and leaves stderr at size 0. That is correct design for a guard. But hc-wrap.sh line 38 pings $BASE/$RC, so a job that exits 1 whenever it has a finding pings /1, and Healthchecks reads any nonzero as a failed run. Two of these three are already wrapped.

CONSEQUENCE: a guard that reports findings by exit status will sit permanently red on the dead-man board, for as long as the finding is open. A board with permanent reds is a board people stop reading, which is LAW 28 — an instrument nobody reads is not an instrument. This is not hypothetical, it is two of the fifteen wrapped jobs today.

I am not fixing it by mapping exit 1 to success, because that throws away the one signal that says a job actually crashed. The distinction the board needs is "did this run" versus "what did it find", and those are two different instruments. I will put the shape up before building it.
